benchmark: AWFL MCP latency - after environment-discovery CLI rollout
test_environment: Production https://api.awfl.us/mcp; fresh shared GKE consumer for awfl-us/server
key_handling: Temporary AWFL MCP key created using Firebase-authenticated API and revoked immediately after each direct run; no keys persisted or logged

methodology.plugin: ChatGPT AWFL Cloud Terminal connector, host-observed Date.now around each complete tool action
methodology.direct: Python requests.Session in the existing GKE consumer to https://api.awfl.us/mcp, using authenticated JSON-RPC initialize/initialized/tools/call
methodology.logs: Cloud Run HTTP request records for ten plugin run_command(yield_time_ms=0) submissions matched by timestamp, from 2026-11-09T15:56:12Z through 15:56:42Z
caveats: Direct client is co-located in GKE while ChatGPT connector runs remotely; differences include gateway, network, host orchestration, and session setup.
The connector's host tool time does not isolate a specific upstream subsystem.
Small samples on warm, shared production infrastructure; no controlled load or confidence intervals.

command_submit_no_wait.operation: run_command with command printf 'ZERO_YIELD_OK\n', yield_time_ms=0 and timeout_ms=30000

plugin_cloud_run_breakdown.note: Stage medians are calculated separately and do not necessarily sum to median overall.

short_command_wait.caution: High variance, shared consumer and nested direct test; not suitable for attributing the entire difference to a single stage.

conclusion: Dominant avoidable user-visible latency for short submissions is before the first HTTP arrival at AWFL Cloud Run. AWS Cloud Run handling still contributes ~418 ms for command submission, while direct authenticated MCP submit takes ~545 ms median.
